title: Caching
subtitle: A cache is a bet that reads repeat
motto: A cache is a bet on repetition
keyInsight: A cache shields the database only while reads repeat within the TTL, and a longer TTL buys hit rate with staleness.

decisions.title: Cache-aside, not write-through
decisions.description: The application reads the cache first and fills it on a miss, so the cache holds only what is actually read and a cache outage makes reads slow rather than failing them.
decisions.alternatives: Write-through keeps the cache fresh, but it writes every row twice, including rows nobody reads back.

decisions.title: Derive hit rate from the TTL
decisions.description: The sim computes the hit rate from how often a key is read and the TTL, so moving the TTL slider changes both database load and staleness.
decisions.alternatives: A fixed hit-rate slider is simpler but hides why the TTL matters, and cannot show the freshness cost.

decisions.title: Model the cold-start failure
decisions.description: The failure frame restarts the cache empty, because a cache that helps on a normal day but sends full load to the database after a restart is the operational risk to learn.
decisions.alternatives: Modeling a single hot-key expiry is closer to a stampede, but it needs a per-key traffic model that would bury the main idea.
